sheet-2-1.description: This part covers North Main Street in the north end of Woodstown, from Grant Street at the left edge to beyond Elm Street and Auburn Street at the right, the upper strip of sheet 2 above the heavy dividing line. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with North Main Street laid out horizontally across the page, so north lies toward the upper right. Grant Street crosses Main at the left edge as an offset crossing, its two halves meeting Main a short distance apart. Elm Street leaves Main toward the bottom of the page, and Auburn Street branches off toward the upper right. The frontages on both sides of Main are almost entirely detached frame dwellings with rear outbuildings, sheds and stables, lettered by lot; a few auto houses and barns stand behind them, and blocks 51, 52 and 55 are numbered. Water pipe sizes and hydrants are marked along Main. Near the bottom of this part, along the heavy line, a wedge of block 55 by Auburn Street is cut off and belongs to the lower strip of the sheet, which continues North Main Street farther north. The part is residential throughout and shows no industrial works or churches.
notes: Grant is today West Grant Street west of Main and East Grant Street east of it; the two halves meet Main about 20 m apart.
Placed from four junctions along North Main Street only (a line of points), so the fit is a similarity transformation.

50 ft. North Main Street north of Grant Street, drawn with Main horizontal (north about 51 deg). Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 Grant Street to Elm and Auburn (above), part 2 Elm to Folwell Street (printed '(No name)') below; same orientation, the strips laid one above the other.

sheet-2-2.description: This part is the lower strip of sheet 2, below the heavy dividing line, and continues North Main Street northward from Elm Street at the left edge to the northern limit of the atlas. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch at the same orientation as the upper strip, with Main running horizontally and north toward the upper right. Auburn Street leaves Main diagonally near the left edge and runs up toward the heavy line, with a fan of narrow lots and dwellings along it, among them an auto repair shop. Along Main the blocks numbered 53 and 54 are lined with detached dwellings on deep lots with stables, sheds and auto houses behind. A street lettered only as having no name leaves Main toward the bottom of the page near the right side; it is today Folwell Street. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad crosses the bottom right corner, with a stand pipe marked beside it. A Princeton University Library map division stamp sits in the lower right of the scan. The part is residential and semi-rural, with open land toward the right and bottom edges marked as having no exposures.
notes: The street printed '(No Name)' leaving Main toward the railroad is today Folwell Street.
Placed from two junctions on North Main Street (Auburn Street and Folwell Street): a two-point similarity transformation, low confidence.

50 ft. North Main Street north of Grant Street, drawn with Main horizontal (north about 51 deg). Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 Grant Street to Elm and Auburn (above), part 2 Elm to Folwell Street (printed '(No name)') below; same orientation, the strips laid one above the other.

sheet-3-1.description: This part shows the large triangular block 2 between North Main Street and Grant Street, north of Bowen Avenue, in the northern part of central Woodstown. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies to the right: Bowen Avenue runs down the left edge, North Main Street runs across the top of the page, bending as it goes, and Grant Street cuts diagonally from Main at the upper right down toward the bottom left. North Main is lined on both sides with detached dwellings with numbered lots, a church at the far left near Bowen Avenue, and a few stores. The interior of the block is largely open, crossed by long lot lines, with dwellings fronting Grant Street on its north side. A row of dwellings faces Bowen Avenue along the left edge. Water pipes are marked along Main and Grant. A heavy line runs along Grant Street and then across the page; the area beyond it, by the railroad, is a separate part of the sheet drawn out of place. Block 55 is numbered beyond the heavy line, and sheet 2 adjoins at the right edge and sheets 4 and 5 at the left.
notes: Grant is today East Grant Street.
Anchored on the junction of North Main and Grant Streets with the atlas scale (8.0 px/ft) and rotation from the measured street lines: low confidence; Bowen Avenue lies just off the left edge.

50 ft, north to the right. Part 1: North Main Street between Bowen Avenue and Grant Street (block 2). Part 2 (below/right of the heavy line along Grant): block 55 by the railroad, Woodstown Ice & Coal Co and Walter Roberts Canning Co, drawn displaced about 95 m from its place relative to part 1; no street junction.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: block 55 by the railroad: Woodstown Ice & Coal Co and Walter Roberts Canning Co, drawn about 95 m out of place (no street junction; railroad tracks only; needs step 6b: carried points from the track layout on sheet 6, or parcel corners).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the centre of Woodstown east of Main Street, from Bowen Avenue at the top to Dickinson Street at the bottom and from Main Street at the left edge to Railroad Avenue at the right, with the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad along the right margin. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. Main Street is cut at the left edge; its east frontage is the commercial core of the town, with brick stores, a hardware store, plumber, the Woodstown Hotel, a drug store, a bank shown as to be built from plans, a furniture store and the Woodstown Monitor-Register printing office. East Avenue crosses the sheet from Main to Railroad Avenue, with the East Avenue Hotel and rows of dwellings on both sides. Between East Avenue and Dickinson Street the middle of the block is open ground marked as a base ball field, crossed by a diagonal lot line. Hitchner and Bassett's coal yard lies by the railroad at Railroad Avenue. Dickinson Street at the bottom is lined with dwellings. Lots are lettered and house numbers are given along each street.
notes: East Avenue is today Harding Highway (US 40).
Railroad Avenue is today East Grant Street north of East Avenue and West Wilson Avenue south of it.
Dickinson Street is today West Dickinson Street.

50 ft, north up. North/South Main Street (cut at the left edge) to Railroad Avenue (today East Grant Street north of East Avenue, West Wilson Avenue south of it), Bowen Avenue to Dickinson Street. East Avenue is today Harding Highway (US 40). Pilot sheet.

sheet-5-1.description: This part covers the west side of central Woodstown around West Avenue, from Main Street at the bottom edge to Salem Creek at the top left, and is the larger part of sheet 5. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the right, so Main Street runs along the bottom and West Avenue climbs diagonally from Main toward the upper left. Greene Street runs up the left edge, with a note that Spring Garden Street continues beyond, and Willow Street runs from it to West Avenue. Along Main Street at the bottom are the commercial buildings of the town centre: stores, a dance hall, the fire department and mayor's office, the post office and the First National Bank near the junction with East Avenue. Along West Avenue are the Harris and Harris garage and the West End Garage, dwellings, a monument works and a tin shop. The Presbyterian church stands near Main at the lower left. A cemetery lies in the middle of the part, and at the top left the Curtice Brothers canning factory number 2, with its warehouse, storage and tomato canning buildings and Italian quarters, sits by Salem Creek.
notes: Greene is today Green Street; Willow appears to be the north end of today's Spring Garden Street at West Avenue.
East Avenue is today Harding Highway (US 40).

Placed from three hand-picked points (Main at West and East Avenues, Greene at Spring Garden and Willow, Willow at West Avenue): an exact fit with no spare point; the detected Greene/West Avenue junction was 16 m off and the parcel centre of the Main/East Avenue junction 16 m from the node, both left out. Low confidence.

50 ft. Part 1 (north to the right): West Avenue, Greene, Willow, Main Street at East Avenue, Curtice Bros canning factory no. 2. Part 2 (north up, right of the heavy line): Dickinson Street to Church Street along Railroad Avenue (West Wilson Avenue), cemeteries, Central Lumber Co.

sheet-5-2.description: This part is the upper right of sheet 5, east of the heavy line, and shows the blocks east of South Main Street between Dickinson Street at the top and Church Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. Railroad Avenue runs down the right edge, with the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad just beyond it. Dickinson Street is lined on its south side with dwellings and the yard of the Central Lumber Company, which has lumber sheds, a planing mill and storage buildings along Railroad Avenue. Below this a large cemetery fills the middle of the block, and Church Street crosses below it, with another cemetery south of Church Street and dwellings along Railroad Avenue on both blocks. Block numbers 8 and 9 are printed. A separate north arrow is drawn for this part, which is set at a different orientation from the rest of the sheet. The lower right of the part is open, and a Princeton University Library map division stamp lies across the corner.
notes: Railroad Avenue is today West Wilson Avenue; Dickinson Street is West Dickinson Street.

Placed from two points, Dickinson Street at Railroad Avenue (detected) and Church Street at Railroad Avenue (hand-picked from the drawn west edge, Railroad Avenue's east side is not drawn): two-point similarity, low confidence.

50 ft. Part 1 (north to the right): West Avenue, Greene, Willow, Main Street at East Avenue, Curtice Bros canning factory no. 2. Part 2 (north up, right of the heavy line): Dickinson Street to Church Street along Railroad Avenue (West Wilson Avenue), cemeteries, Central Lumber Co.

sheet-6-1.description: Sheet 6 covers the east side of Woodstown along the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, north of East Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. Railroad Avenue lies along the left edge, the railroad tracks with sidings run up the left third of the page, and Broadway runs north from East Avenue to Elm Street, which crosses the top right corner diagonally. By the tracks stand the Supplee-Wills-Jones Milk Company receiving station, the passenger station and freight house, the South Jersey Farmers Exchange fertilizer manufactory and warehouse, a feed warehouse and the John E. Watson farm implement warehouse. Along Broadway there are a few dwellings, a Roman Catholic church and a long horse shed. East Avenue runs along the bottom, with a street printed as having no name and School Street leaving it southward. The upper right of the page is largely open land behind Elm Street, and a boxed inset of the public school block occupies the middle right; it is a separate part.
notes: Broadway is today Broad Street; East Avenue is Harding Highway (US 40).
The street printed '(No Name) Street' south of East Avenue is today Wilson Avenue; School (Arbity) Street is today Lincoln Avenue.
All six control points lie along East Avenue (a line), so the fit is a similarity transformation; Broadway at Elm Street lies just off the top edge.

50 ft, north up. Part 1: Broadway (Broad Street) and the railroad north of East Avenue (Harding Highway), Elm Street, South Jersey Farmers Exchange, Supplee-Wills-Jones milk station. Part 2: boxed inset of block 58, Public School at East Avenue and School (Arbity) Street (today Lincoln Avenue).

sheet-6-2.description: This part is the boxed inset on sheet 6 showing block 58, the public school block, on the south side of East Avenue east of School Street. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, pointing up, and is placed on the page away from its true position. East Avenue, 60 feet wide, runs across the top of the box, and School Street, printed with the alternative name Arbity and 50 feet wide, runs down its left side. The block itself is mostly open, with the Public School, a brick building with stairs, a boiler room and a manual training shop, at its lower right. The edges of the box are marked as having no exposures. Water pipes are shown in East Avenue. The inset adds nothing else; the streets around it are drawn on sheets 6 and 7.
notes: School (Arbity) Street is today Lincoln Avenue; East Avenue is Harding Highway (US 40).
Anchored on the junction of East Avenue and School Street with the scale and rotation of the main part of the sheet: low confidence.

50 ft, north up. Part 1: Broadway (Broad Street) and the railroad north of East Avenue (Harding Highway), Elm Street, South Jersey Farmers Exchange, Supplee-Wills-Jones milk station. Part 2: boxed inset of block 58, Public School at East Avenue and School (Arbity) Street (today Lincoln Avenue).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the west side of South Main Street south of the town centre, between Allen Avenue at the left and Greene Street and Dickinson Street at the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the right. South Main Street runs across the lower middle of the page and Spring Garden Street parallel to it near the top, with Hunt Street joining the two and Church Street leaving Main toward the bottom. The blocks are residential, with detached dwellings and outbuildings on numbered lots. Along South Main stand the Asbury Methodist Episcopal church, the First Baptist church with its chapel, a public library and several stores. The City Water Works pump house, with its duplex pumps, stands at the top left beyond Spring Garden Street. The Baptist cemetery fills the lower right, and Salem Creek crosses the lower left corner. Block numbers 6, 7, 8 and 12 are printed.
notes: Greene is today Green Street; Dickinson is West Dickinson Street.
50 ft, north to the right. South Main Street and Spring Garden Street between Allen Avenue and Greene Street, Hunt and Church Streets, Baptist church and cemetery, City Water Works pump house.

sheet-8-1.description: This part covers South Main Street where it crosses Salem Creek at the south end of Woodstown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the right. South Main Street runs across the upper middle of the page and crosses the creek on a concrete bridge; Allen Avenue leaves Main upward near the right, and Mill Street and Creamery Street leave Main at nearly the same point near the middle, Mill Street climbing to the upper left and Creamery Street running down to the lower right. The creek winds from the top of the page down to the right edge. Along Main are dwellings, a hardware store, a blacksmith, a woodworking shop with a gasoline engine and a cider mill. Samuel H. Weatherby's lumber yard with its lumber sheds lies between Creamery Street and the creek, along a railroad siding. At the bottom right the Curtice Brothers canning factory number 1 stands by the railroad with its process building and storage and packing houses. Block numbers 9, 10, 11 and 12 are printed. A boxed inset at the lower left is a separate part.
notes: Mill Street is today West Millbrooke Avenue (the modern Mill Street is its continuation to the south); Creamery Street is today East Millbrooke Avenue.

Anchored on the hand-picked junction of Main, Mill and Creamery Streets with the atlas scale (8.0 px/ft) and a rotation of 86 degrees; the detected Allen Avenue junction lies about 5 m from this placement. Low confidence.

50 ft, north to the right. Part 1: South Main Street across Salem Creek, Mill Street (today West Millbrooke Avenue), Creamery Street (today East Millbrooke Avenue), Allen Avenue, Curtice Bros canning factory no. 1. Part 2: boxed inset, former site of East Lake Roller Mill, 1 mile SE of the post office; no streets.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: former site of East Lake Roller Mill, 1 mile SE of the post office (no street or other feature shared with the modern data; needs parcel corners or a building surviving at the site).

sheet-9-1.description: This part covers South Main Street south of Water Street at the southern edge of Woodstown, together with Water Street running west across the top of the sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. South Main runs down the right side of the page, bending at Water Street, and is lined on both sides with dwellings on deep lots; the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) crosses Main diagonally in the lower half. The Methodist cemetery lies west of Main behind the dwellings. Water Street, 35 feet wide, runs along the top strip of the page with dwellings, a blacksmith and the Daniels and Gilbert auto painting shop. Block numbers 10, 11 and 50 are printed. The left side and bottom of the page beyond the heavy line belong to a separate part drawn at another orientation.
notes: Water Street is today Lotus Avenue.
Placed from the hand-picked junction of Main and Water Streets and the detected railroad crossing on Main: two-point similarity, low confidence.

50 ft. Part 1 (north about 41 deg): South Main Street south of Water Street (today Lotus Avenue) to the railroad crossing, Water Street west to Mill Street, Methodist cemetery. Part 2 (north about 10 deg, left of the heavy line): Mill Street (today West Millbrooke Avenue and Mill Street) south across Salem Creek to Water Street, Davis & Lippincott canning factory, Foster Bros.

sheet-9-2.description: This part, left of the heavy line on sheet 9, shows Mill Street south of the town where it crosses Salem Creek, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing up and set at a different angle from the rest of the sheet. Mill Street enters along the top as a 30 foot street, turns a corner and runs down the left side of the page, 35 feet wide, crossing Salem Creek on a culvert. Most of the ground east of Mill Street is open, block 11, with a few dwellings and an auto repairing and feed mill building to the west. At the bottom the Davis and Lippincott canning factory, with skinning, machine, packing and storage rooms, stands where Mill Street meets Water Street, which runs diagonally up to the right; the Foster Brothers garage and dwellings stand south of Water Street. Block number 50 is printed at the bottom.
notes: Mill Street here is today West Millbrooke Avenue (the upper arm) and Mill Street (the arm running south); Water Street is today Lotus Avenue.

Anchored on the hand-picked junction of Mill and Water Streets with the atlas scale (8.0 px/ft) and a rotation of 10 degrees from Mill Street's drawn direction; the corner of Mill Street falls between the modern junction and bend. Low confidence.

50 ft. Part 1 (north about 41 deg): South Main Street south of Water Street (today Lotus Avenue) to the railroad crossing, Water Street west to Mill Street, Methodist cemetery.
